task.description: WF-03 Step 4: write a regression test proving Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_realm/1 (new function, added by this branch's fix) is built on Ecto.UUID.generate/0 rather than a process-local counter. The original bug is a cross-process/cross-VM race inherently un-reproducible on demand within one test run, so the test proves the fix's discriminating property (UUID-format suffix) instead, and -- per WF-03's 'pre-fix failure is code-does-not-exist' rule -- a mutation was applied and measured since a bare pre-fix-commit check would only prove the function was new, not that the tests discriminate correct-vs-broken.

summary: Added 3 test cases to the existing Letflow.TenantSlugFixtureTest module (test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs), under a new describe block 'unique_realm/1 uses a UUID suffix, not a process-local counter (ISS-0878)': (1) a StreamData property asserting no duplicates across 1,000 in-process calls (baseline sanity, not alone sufficient); (2) a StreamData property regex-matching the generated suffix against the exact Ecto.UUID.generate/0 format across 30 randomized (prefix, repeat_count) pairs -- the discriminating assertion; (3) a unit test covering the zero-argument default-prefix ('realm') call path.

Confirmed via direct read of git diff origin/main...feature/WF03-ISS0878-20260929 -- test/ that all 4 call sites (auth_pipeline_test.exs, authorization_ac9_test.exs, provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs, identity_test.exs) delegate to Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_realm/1 rather than keeping their own counter-based copy -- lightweight confirmation per the design doc's own scoping, not a new test (already checked by REVIEWER in step-04).
BASELINE (pre-mutant, current correct implementation): `mix test test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 7.9 seconds (7.9s async, 0.00s sync)' / 'Result: 9 passed (4 properties, 5 tests)'.

MUTANT APPLIED (WF-03 non-existence-case rule, in-place technique): test/support/tenant_slug.ex's unique_realm/1 body temporarily changed to the pre-fix buggy pattern `"#{prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}"`.

MUTANT RESULT: `mix test test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs` -> 'Result: 7/9 passed (3/4 properties, 4/5 tests)' / 'Failed: 1 property, 1 test'. The two failing tests were exactly the two UUID-format-discriminating assertions added by this run: 'default prefix ("realm") also gets a UUID-format suffix' (got 'realm-1005', a bare integer suffix) and 'the generated suffix matches the Ecto.UUID.generate/0 format' (got suffix '1028', failing the UUID regex). The two non-format assertions (uniqueness-only, prefix-only) still passed under the mutant, as expected -- confirming the added coverage is sensitive to exactly the UUID-vs-counter trap ISS-0878 fixes, not merely present.

REVERT VERIFIED: `git status --porcelain test/ lib/` returned only ' M test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs' (this run's own new test file) -- test/support/tenant_slug.ex confirmed back to pristine branch content, nothing under lib/ touched at any point.
POST-REVERT RE-RUN (green, matches baseline exactly): `mix test test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 7.5 seconds (7.5s async, 0.00s sync)' / 'Result: 9 passed (4 properties, 5 tests)'.

Additional check: `touch test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs && mix test test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs --warnings-as-errors` forces a fresh recompile; result still 'Result: 9 passed (4 properties, 5 tests)', and the run aborted on --warnings-as-errors only due to the pre-existing, already-deferred ISS-0044 Group 1 ExUnit.Case.register_test/4 deprecation warning (documented in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex's own moduledoc as a known, permanently-deferred class blocked on a stream_data version bump) -- no new warning, and no dead-default-argument (ISS-0069 class) warning, since this run introduced no new defp with an optional/default argument.
